data.name: Rag GTPases
data.description: Family of small GTPases that let mTORC1 sense amino acids by controlling its localization near its activator Rheb inside the cell.
data.description_beginner: A family of small molecular switches that let mTORC1 sense amino acids by controlling where inside the cell it's allowed to sit - specifically, whether it can get close enough to its activator Rheb.

studies.title: ER-Lysosome Cholesterol Exchange Regulates Lysosomal Motility Through mTOR-Dependent LAMTOR1 Phosphorylation
studies.authors: Muthukottiappan P; Winter D et al.

studies.title: Ragulator-Rag complex targets mTORC1 to the lysosomal surface and is necessary for its activation by amino acids
studies.authors: Sancak Y; Bar-Peled L; Zoncu R; Markhard AL; Nada S; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Established WHERE mTORC1 gets switched on: the lysosome surface. Identified Ragulator as the lysosomal dock that recruits the Rag GTPases and drags mTORC1 to the membrane where its activator Rheb lives. Amino acids work by controlling this translocation.

studies.title: mTORC1 senses lysosomal amino acids through an inside-out mechanism that requires the vacuolar H(+)-ATPase
studies.authors: Zoncu R; Bar-Peled L; Efeyan A; Wang S; Sancak Y; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed amino acid sensing starts INSIDE the lysosome: amino acids accumulate in the lumen and the v-ATPase relays that signal outward ('inside-out') to Ragulator-Rag. A surprising twist on where the cell measures its nutrient status.

studies.title: A Tumor suppressor complex with GAP activity for the Rag GTPases that signal amino acid sufficiency to mTORC1
studies.authors: Bar-Peled L; Chantranupong L; Cherniack AD; Chen WW; Ottina KA; Grabiner BC; Spear ED; Carter SL; Meyerson M; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Found the OFF switch for amino acid signaling: the GATOR1 complex is a GAP that shuts the Rag GTPases (and thus mTORC1) down when amino acids run low, while GATOR2 opposes it. GATOR1 genes are mutated in cancers, making those tumors 'blind' to starvation and hypersensitive to rapamycin.

studies.title: Structure of the lysosomal mTORC1-TFEB-Rag-Ragulator megacomplex
studies.authors: Cui Z; Napolitano G; de Araujo MEG; Esposito A; Monfregola J; Huber LA; Ballabio A; Hurley JH

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: First structural view of how mTORC1 actually reaches TFEB to phosphorylate it: two full Rag-Ragulator complexes present a single TFEB molecule to the mTOR active site, one in the normal Raptor-docking arrangement and a second, non-canonical one that grips TFEB's own first helix. Mutating that grip point drives TFEB straight into the nucleus (turning on autophagy/lysosome genes) without disturbing where mTORC1 itself sits. Explains, at the level of atoms, why TFEB phosphorylation needs the tumour suppressor FLCN and the GDP-loaded state of RagC in a way no other mTORC1 substrate does. Boundary: cryo-EM of a complex reconstituted from purified human proteins — a static structural snapshot, not a live cell or a real-time measurement.

studies.title: Structural basis for mTORC1 activation on the lysosomal membrane
studies.authors: Cui Z; Esposito A; Napolitano G; Ballabio A; Hurley JH

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Cryo-EM structure (human proteins, reconstituted on membranes) + validation in inducible RAPTOR-KO MEFs
studies.finding: Resolves how mTORC1 flips from 'parked on the lysosome' to 'catalytically switched on'. Reconstituting the whole assembly on membranes from purified Rheb, Rag GTPases, Ragulator and mTORC1, cryo-EM shows the kinase reaches full activity only after two separate anchoring steps: Rag-Ragulator first pulls it to within about 100 angstroms of the membrane, then Rheb pulls it to within about 40 angstroms, and only when Raptor and mTOR itself also touch the membrane directly do the catalytic residues line up for full activity. Growth-factor input (via Rheb) and nutrient input (via the Rags) are shown converging on the same physical docking event rather than acting through separate switches. Boundary: reconstituted on synthetic membranes from purified components — a structural/biochemical model, not a measurement inside a living cell.

studies.title: Structural basis for the docking of mTORC1 on the lysosomal surface
studies.authors: Rogala KB; Sabatini DM et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Cryo-EM structure (human proteins, cell-free reconstitution) + cell-based mutagenesis
studies.finding: 3.2-angstrom cryo-EM structure of Raptor bound to Rag-Ragulator, showing how Raptor reads out the nutrient-dependent nucleotide state of the Rag GTPases: one part of Raptor senses RagA's nucleotide state, a separate 'claw' senses RagC's, and both have to be in the correct nutrient-signalling combination before Raptor is allowed to dock. Mutating the contact points blocks mTORC1 from reaching the lysosome and inhibits its signalling, which is the functional evidence behind the structural claim. Combined with a separate structure of mTORC1 bound to its activator Rheb, the paper builds a model of the complete, active mTORC1 sitting on the lysosome. Boundary: cryo-EM of a complex reconstituted from purified human proteins, not a live-cell measurement.

studies.title: Spatial coupling of mTOR and autophagy augments secretory phenotypes
studies.authors: Narita Masako; Young AR; Arakawa S; Samarajiwa SA; Nakashima T; Yoshida S; Hong S; Berry LS; Reichelt S; Ferreira M; Tavare S; Inoki K; Shimizu S; Narita Masashi

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human and mouse cells (Ras-induced senescent fibroblasts, macrophages, podocytes)
studies.finding: Protein synthesis and autophagic degradation are usually described as opposites that mTOR switches between, and this paper shows a compartment where the cell deliberately runs both at once. In senescent cells, autolysosomes and mTOR gather at one side of the Golgi (the TASCC), mTOR gets there in an amino-acid- and Rag-dependent way, and destroying that arrangement cuts interleukin-6/8 secretion. Boundary: cells, not organisms; it explains how the senescent secretory programme is fuelled, not whether blocking it helps an animal.

studies.title: Synergistic role of TFEB/TFE3 and mTORC1 in kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis
studies.authors: Ferniani M; Sambri I; Huynh T; Pennella R; Tufano G; Herz NJ; Rossi B; Iannaccone A; Trepiccione F; Calcagnì A; Ballabio A

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Kidney-specific conditional knockout mice: Depdc5-KO, RagC-KO, and Flcn/RagC double-KO (models of Birt-Hogg-Dube and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex)
studies.finding: Using kidney-specific mouse models that genetically uncouple mTORC1 activity from TFEB/TFE3 activity (Depdc5-KO, RagC-KO, and Flcn/RagC double-KO), the authors show mTORC1 hyperactivation -- not TFEB/TFE3 activation alone -- is the primary driver of kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis in Birt-Hogg-Dube and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex models. Constitutive TFEB/TFE3 activity further accelerates disease on top of mTORC1-driven pathology.

studies.title: Substrate-selective mTORC1 regulation and gene dosage-dependent tissue divergence in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome
studies.authors: Cao ZL; Zhao SC; Lin F; Liu YH; Hong XT; Hong LY; Xu LQ; Li FP; Yu HY; Yao WG; Chen WY

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Narrative synthesis (human genetics + mouse mechanistic data)
studies.finding: Reframes Birt-Hogg-Dube (BHD) syndrome beyond the classic 'global mTORC1 hyperactivation' model: FLCN acts as a GAP for RagC/D, giving substrate-selective (not global) mTORC1 control. Biallelic FLCN loss drives kidney tumors via MiT/TFE nuclear accumulation, while haploinsufficiency alone is sufficient for lung and skin lesions -- resolving the 'mTORC1 paradox' via gene dosage and signaling timing. Narrative synthesis of human genetics and mouse mechanistic data.

studies.title: A Rag GTPase dimer code defines the regulation of mTORC1 by amino acids
studies.authors: Gollwitzer P; Grützmacher N; Wilhelm S; Kümmel D; Demetriades C

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human cells (genetically modified Rag-paralogue cell lines)
studies.finding: The four mammalian Rag GTPase paralogues are not functionally interchangeable: RagC/D determines substrate specificity (RagD favors TFEB/TFE3 phosphorylation via tighter LAMTOR binding), while RagA/B determines the response to amino acid withdrawal (RagB-expressing cells keep mTORC1 lysosomal and active even upon starvation). Author correction issued 2023 (PMID 36536178, no change to conclusions).

studies.title: Ragulator and SLC38A9 activate the Rag GTPases through noncanonical GEF mechanisms
studies.authors: Shen K; Sabatini DM
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Ragulator and SLC38A9 each act as an unusual guanine-nucleotide exchange factor on the Rag heterodimer, and together they push it into its active state. Ragulator triggers GTP release from RagC, which unlocks the inactive configuration; arginine-bound SLC38A9 converts RagA from the GDP- to the GTP-loaded state. Boundary: purified proteins and cultured human cells. This is the biochemistry of the switch, not a measurement in tissue.

relations.mechanism: FLCN-FNIP is the GAP for the other half of the Rag dimer (RagC/D). Only when both halves are in the right nucleotide state can the dimer hold mTORC1. Crucially this arm is SUBSTRATE-SPECIFIC: it gates TFEB and TFE3 phosphorylation, while canonical outputs like S6K1 and 4E-BP1 carry on without it.
relations.mechanism_beginner: FLCN flips the other half of the Rag pair into its working shape – but it only changes one specific output (TFEB), not the whole pathway.
relations.boundary: The substrate selectivity is why Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome is driven by constitutive nuclear TFEB/TFE3 rather than by blanket mTORC1 hyperactivation (NAP2020).

relations.mechanism: GATOR1 acts as a GAP: it forces RagA/B to hydrolyse GTP, flipping the Rag heterodimer into the inactive shape that cannot hold mTORC1.
relations.mechanism_beginner: GATOR1 forces the Rag proteins into their "off" shape, so they can no longer hold onto mTORC1.

relations.mechanism: Glutamine burned through glutaminolysis raises alpha-ketoglutarate, which promotes RagB GTP loading and mTORC1 translocation to the lysosome. This edge asserts the Rag-dependent route only.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Glutamine can switch on mTORC1 partly just by being burned for fuel: burning it makes a molecule that helps the Rag proteins pull mTORC1 to the lysosome.
relations.boundary: Cell-type dependent, and deliberately narrow: the separate claim that glutamine can reach mTORC1 without the Rags is carried by its own edge rather than folded in here.
relations.note: Split from the Rag-independent claim on 2026-09-13 after external review: one edge was asserting a Rag-dependent mechanism and describing a Rag-independent one in the same sentence.

relations.mechanism: In this model LARS acts as a GAP for RagD, doing for the RagC/D half what FLCN does - an alternative route from leucine to the Rags.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In that model, this enzyme flips the other Rag protein into its working shape – an alternative route from leucine to the Rags.
relations.boundary: Human cell biochemistry only, and cell-type dependence was never mapped. The reaction it claims - GAP activity on the RagC/D half - is the same reaction this Atlas assigns to FLCN, and the two assignments have never been reconciled head-to-head. Read together with LEU-LARS: if the upstream leucine-sensing claim does not hold, this edge loses its input.

relations.mechanism: The active Rag dimer grabs Raptor and physically drags mTORC1 to the lysosomal surface. This is a relocation, not an activation - the kinase is moved to where its activator waits.
relations.mechanism_beginner: The switched-on Rag proteins grab mTORC1 and drag it to the lysosome. This moves it into place; it doesn't turn it on by itself.
relations.boundary: Rag paralogues are not interchangeable: RagC/D sets substrate specificity downstream (RagD favors TFEB/TFE3 phosphorylation via tighter LAMTOR binding, while both Rags are involved for non-lysosomal substrates like S6K), and RagA/B sets the response to amino acid withdrawal (RagB-expressing cells keep mTORC1 lysosomal and active even when starved) — GOL2022.
relations.note: The conceptual crux of the whole route: teach recruitment vs activation as two separate ideas.

relations.mechanism: Ragulator does two jobs on the Rags. It tethers the Rag heterodimer to the lysosomal surface, and it acts as an unusual exchange factor: first reported as a GEF for RagA/B (BAR2012), its exchange activity was later placed on RagC, where releasing GTP unlocks the inactive state (SHE2018B). Loading RagA with GTP is done by arginine-bound SLC38A9 (see SLC38A9-RAG).
relations.mechanism_beginner: Ragulator anchors the Rag proteins to the lysosome and also helps flip them into their "on" shape, together with a second protein, SLC38A9. Both jobs are shown in biochemical experiments.

relations.mechanism: SLC38A9 sits in the lysosomal membrane and reads arginine on the inside. Arginine-bound SLC38A9 acts as an exchange factor that loads RagA with GTP, switching the Rag dimer on (SHE2018B); it also pumps essential amino acids, including leucine, back out into the cytosol.
relations.mechanism_beginner: SLC38A9 sits in the lysosome's wall, senses arginine inside, and then flips RagA into its "on" shape, telling the Rag proteins there's enough.
relations.note: Five independent studies - one of the best-supported edges in the sensor branch.

relations.mechanism: When amino acids run out, the Rag GTPases also pull the TSC complex onto the lysosome, where it can switch Rheb off and help shut mTORC1 down.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Without amino acids, the Rags bring the TSC brake to the lysosome.
relations.boundary: Mammalian cell lines under acute amino-acid withdrawal; the contribution of this route in tissues is not established. Single study.
